buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE 25% : The buyer can increase or decrease the contract quantity or contract duration up to 25 percent at the time of issue of the contract. However, once the contract is issued, the contract quantity or contract duration can only be increased up to 25 percent. Bidders are bound to accept the revised quantity or duration. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 25 percent with the consent of the service provider 2. Generic

1. The Seller shall not assign the Contract in whole or part without obtaining the prior written consent of buyer. 2. The Seller shall not sub-contract the Contract in whole or part to any entity without obtaining the prior written consent of buyer. 3. The Seller shall, notwithstanding the consent and assignment/sub-contract, remain jointly and severally liable and responsible to buyer together with the assignee/ sub-contractor, for and in respect of the due performance of the Contract and the Sellers obligations there under. 3. Purchase Preference (Centre) Preference to Make In India products (For bids less than 200 Crore):Preference shall be given to Class 1 local supplier as defined in public procurement (Preference to Make in India), Order 2017 as amended from time to time and its subsequent Orders/Notifications issued by concerned Nodal Ministry for specific Goods/Products. The minimum local content to qualify as a Class 1 local supplier is denoted in the bid document 50%. If the bidder wants to avail the Purchase preference, the bidder must upload a certificate from the OEM regarding the percentage of the local content and the details of locations at which the local value addition is made along with their bid, failing which no purchase preference shall be granted. In case the bid value is more than Rs 10 Crore, the declaration relating to percentage of local content shall be certified by the statutory auditor or cost auditor, if the OEM is a company and by a practicing cost accountant or a chartered accountant for OEMs other than companies as per the Public Procurement (preference to Make-in -India) order 2017 dated 04.06.2020. Only Class-I and Class-II Local suppliers as per MII order dated 4.6.2020 will be eligible to bid. Non - Local suppliers as per MII order dated 04.06.2020 are not eligible to participate. In case Buyer has selected Purchase preference to Micro and Small Enterprises clause in the bid, the same will get precedence over this clause. 4. Purchase Preference (Centre) Preference to Make In India products (for bids greater than 200 Crore) (can also be used in Bids less than 200 Crore but only after exemption by competent authority as defined in Deptt of Expenditure OM dated 28.5.2020): Preference shall be given to Class 1 local supplier as defined in public procurement (Preference to Make in India), Order 2017 as amended from time to time and its subsequent Orders/Notifications issued by concerned Nodal Ministry for specific Goods/Products. The minimum local content to qualify as a Class 1 local supplier is denoted in the bid document 50%. If the bidder wants to avail the Purchase preference, the bidder must upload a certificate from the OEM regarding the percentage of the local content and the details of locations at which the local value addition is made along with their bid, failing which no purchase preference shall be granted. In case the bid value is more than Rs 10 Crore, the declaration relating to percentage of local content shall be certified by the statutory auditor or cost auditor, if the OEM is a company and by a practicing cost accountant or a chartered accountant for OEMs other than companies as per the Public Procurement (preference to Make-in -India) order 2017 dated 04.06.2020. In case Buyer has selected Purchase preference to Micro and Small Enterprises clause in the bid, the same will get precedence over this clause. 5. Purchase Preference (Centre) Procurement under this bid is reserved for purchase from Micro and Small Enterprises whose credentials are validated online through Udyog Aadhaar/URC for that product/service category. If the bidder wants to avail the reservation benefit, the bidder must be the manufacturer of the offered product in case of bid for supply of goods. Traders are excluded from the purview of Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises. In respect of bid for Services, the bidder must be the Service provider of the offered Service. Relevant documentary evidence in this regard shall be uploaded along with the bid in respect of the offered product or service. 6. Service & Support AVAILABILITY OF OFFICE OF SERVICE PROVIDER: An office of the Service Provider must be located in the state of Consignee. DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE TO BE SUBMITTED. 7. Service & Support Dedicated /toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support : BIDDER/OEM must have Dedicated/toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support. 8. Service & Support

Escalation Matrix For Service Support : Bidder/OEM must provide Escalation Matrix of Telephone Numbers for Service Support. 9. Certificates Bidder's offer is liable to be rejected if they don't upload any of the certificates / documents sought in the Bid document, ATC and Corrigendum if any. 10. Any other document in support of contract execution like Third Party Inspection release note, etc.Proof for Past Experience and Project Experience clause: For fulfilling the experience criteria any one of the following documents may be considered as valid proof for meeting the experience criteria:a. Geographical Presence: The bidder should have registered office in Madhya Pradesh (supportive documen t must be uploaded). 2. Compulsory attendance is required in pre-bid interaction. The bidder absenting from pre-bid meeting will not be entertained and summarily rejected. 3. Bidder’s financial standing: - The bidder should not be under liquidation, court receivership or any other similar proceedings and should n ot be bankrupt. Bidder has to upload undertaking to this effect along with its bid. 4. Clearance of bills complete in all aspects can take 3-4 months after submission due to non-availability of f unds. The bidder should be financially strong to pay the monthly wages to their employees in time (within 7 th day of subsequent month). Declaration of the same must be submitted by the bidder. No ground of bidde r for non-payment of wages to the outsource employees will be entertained in any manner. 5. The bidder must submit an undertaking for compliance of minimum wages as prescribed by the Central G overnment. 6. Duration of the service/contract may be extended up to 3 months beyond the initial contract duration (su bject to satisfactory performance and mutual consent). 7. The bidder shall not assign the Contract in whole or part without obtaining the prior written consent of bu yer. 8. The bidder shall not sub-contract the Contract in whole or part to any entity without obtaining the prior wr itten consent of buyer. 9. The Bidder shall, notwithstanding the consent and assignment/sub-contract, remain jointly and severally li able and responsible to buyer together with the assignee/ sub-contractor, for and in respect of the due perf ormance of the Contract and the Sellers obligations there under. 10. Bidder should have Private Security Regulation Act (PASARA), 2005, License issued by Government of Mad hya Pradesh/Competent Authority. The license should be valid on the date of application. Pending applicati on for approval/renewal would not be considered i.e. in other words if the bidder has applied for license or r enewal thereof which is pending then the same would not be considered. 11. The Bidder must file the default of incidents. including incidents where it has been blacklisted from any ea rlier contract or agreement an undertaking to this effect must be submitted by the bidder. 12. Service provider shall ensure the all-relevant licenses/registration/permission which may be required for p roviding the Security/Manpower services are valid during the entire period of the contract. 13. Successful Bidder must submit/upload an undertaking in respect of no criminal cases/inquiry is pending or contemplated against the bidder across India including that of Income Tax Department. 14. The bidder must be registered with GST, EPFO and ESIC Documentary evidence must be uploaded. 15. Successful Bidder shall provide salary slip with bifurcation of all deduction every month during entire contr

act period. Proof of payment of salary along with deposit of PF& ESI as applicable must be given along with monthly bill duly certified by the bidder. 16. The successful Bidder shall not have any right to change any outsource personnel without prior approval o f the buyer during entire contract period considering information security norms. 17. Successful bidder will provide the Identity Cards to the deployed personnel at his own cost. 18. In case the successful bidder default in providing services and make discrepancies /fault found from succ essful bidder a Show Cause Notice/Notice/ letter will be issued. If in the successful bidder fails to give satisf actory reply, then appropriate action may be taken by Competent Authority including change of personnel, penalties, dissolution of contract, blacklisting etc. 19. Successful bidder must file an undertaking that no police case/ enquiry is pending against the personnel s upplied under this contract to this department. 20. The outsourced staff must observe all the etiquettes and protocol while performing the duty. He must be n eatly dressed, should wear proper uniform and must carry mobile phone in working condition, for which no separate payment shall be made by the department. 21. The successful bidder would be required to generate bill through online GeM portal wherein physical copie s of attendance register PF, ESIC etc needs to be uploaded. 22. Documentary proof regarding the bidder fulfilling all eligible conditions must be uploaded. 23. Bidder as all above listed ATC plays an important role in successful bidder. 24. It may be noted that payment will be restricted to the actual working days only. 25. The Pr.CIT-1, Indore reserves the right to reject any of the bid/quotations without quoting any reason. . 12. Payment PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND WAGES: Service Provider is required to pay Salaries / wages of contracted staff deployed at buyer location first i.e. on their own and then claim payment from Buyer alongwith all statutory documents like, PF, ESIC etc. as well as the bank statement of payment done to staff.
